messages:
Alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector roll (kv-match priority) our 99th p95 tail on hosted small-chat workloads crept ~12%. Profiling shows host-side cost, not GPU. Looks like tokenization + framing amplification.
Maria: Which canary id? and model?
Alex: canary=canary-7f, model=redwood-open-7b-v2, traffic ~5%. I captured a short flame and socket trace.
Alex: ```
HOST CPU slices (top):
 - tokenize: 34%
 - grpc_writev: 21%
 - req_parse/deserialize: 18%
 - kv_cache_eviction: 9%
 notes: lots of tiny writev bursts, many ~256B.```
Sasha: tiny write bursts smell http2/HPACK + small frames. Did kernel-selector change increase average batch size?
Alex: yes — batching heuristics now favor >2x batch aggregation to improve GPU throughput. That increased serialization time per request; we see more prefix coalescing causing heavier host prep.
Dave: I pushed a local patch that reuses a single iovec buffer across streaming chunks to avoid repeated allocations. That cut tokenize->write syscalls by ~30% in my microbench.
Maria: Interesting — also see kv cache churn. Larger batches mean longer KV cache hold times, evicting hot entries for very long sessions.
Alex: Right. KV hit rate drops for long chats, which forces more host-side reconstruction of KV slices. Combined with smaller writes, the net is worse.
perf-bot: Regression alert: 2026-03-19 14:12 UTC - p99 latency +12% on canary-7f (link: https://perf/redwood/alerts/9876) :loud_sound:
Sasha: Short term: can we clamp batch size for low-latency routes? e.g. max_batch_tokens=1024 and stream_coalesce_threshold=512. That keeps GPU util but reduces host serialization windows.
Dave: Agree. Also adding a writev coalescer at the proxy layer reduces the number of frames when chunk sizes are small — I can prototype.
Maria: For KV: change eviction policy to favor session affinity (LRU -> seg-lru with session bias) for dedicated routes. Might help hot-chat stickiness.
Alex: Action items:
 - Dave: prototype writev coalescer + reuse buffer (Dave -> PR draft)
 - Sasha: experiment with batch_clamp + stream_coalesce (toggle via runtime flag)
 - Maria: simulate KV eviction policy change on replay harness to check hit-rate
 - Alex: hold kernel-selector rollout on more canaries until we verify
Sasha: Any quick mitigations we can flip in prod right now?
Dave: I can flip a feature flag to reduce max_aggregate_batches for low-tier routes; simple and safe.
Alex: Do that; monitor p99 and kv-hit. If it stabilizes, we revert selector tweak or iterate heuristics.
Maria: I'll add a regression test that runs long-session replay for 10k tokens to catch KV thrash.
Sasha: I'll add a shorttrace to capture writev-size distribution; need that to validate coalescer effect.
Alex: Thanks. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:
Dave: PR up at https://git/repo/pull/4521 (wip) — includes buffer reuse microbench numbers.
perf-bot: Note: schedule a canary rollback window if p99 > +8% for 30m.
Maria: will do replay tomorrow morning and post numbers.
Alex: Closing loop: if coalescer + batch_clamp recovers <+3% tail and kv-hit > baseline-1%, we can continue kernel selector on slow ramp.
Sasha: copy.
Maria: ping when replay completes.
Dave: landing draft for review.
Alex: good work team:
